Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on an official visit to Qatar from 27 to 29 September 2026
articles.full_content:
Union Finance Minister will attend the 11th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) during the visit The Union Finance Minister Smt. Sitharaman will also hold important bilateral meetings with the AIIB President and her counterparts including from Jordan, Switzerland, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, and Nepal
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on an official visit to Qatar from 27 th to 29 th September, 2026. The Union Finance Minister is leading the delegation comprising of Ministry of Finance officials.
During the visit, Smt. Sitharaman will attend the 11 th Annual Meeting of Board of Governors of Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) scheduled in Doha on 28 th September 2026, besides other important bilateral meetings with the AIIB President and her counterparts from Jordan, Switzerland, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, and Nepal.
In the Annual Meeting of AIIB, the Union Finance Minister will attend as the Indian Governor to the AIIB. India is the second largest shareholder of the bank.
As part of the official visit, the Union Finance Minister is expected to call-on the leadership of the Government of Qatar, and also engage with Qatari business leaders and investors.
About AIIB and Annual Meetings
The AIIB Annual Meeting witnesses participation of delegations from member countries, and other international organisations. As a multilateral development bank, AIIB is focused on developing sustainable infrastructure in Asia and in promoting investments in infrastructure and other productive sectors with the aim to foster sustainable economic development, create wealth and improve infrastructure connectivity.

ICAR Institutes Promote Cleanliness and Sustainable Waste Management
articles.full_content:
As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva activities, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) organised awareness and cleanliness initiatives focused on post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness, clean public spaces and responsible waste management at ICAR institutions. The initiatives aimed to promote environmental protection, safe practices and community participation in maintaining clean surroundings after Ganesh Visarjan.
An awareness programme on post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness was organised at a local Ganesh pandal, where participants were sensitised about the use of eco-friendly clay idols and advised to avoid immersion of Plaster of Paris idols and idols containing harmful chemical colours in drinking water tanks. Participants were encouraged to use designated immersion sites and avoid immersing idols and Puja Samagri in natural water bodies. Emphasis was also laid on proper collection and disposal of flowers, Puja Samagri, plastic, thermocol and other decorative waste.
The programme also highlighted the importance of maintaining cleanliness at immersion sites, preventing littering and following safety precautions near water bodies. The areas surrounding the local Ganesh pandal were cleaned, with garbage collected and segregated to facilitate safe and responsible waste management. The initiative highlighted the importance of collective responsibility and community participation in protecting water resources and maintaining clean public spaces.
As part of the activities, biodegradable offerings including flowers and other Puja Samagri were collected and segregated at ICAR-NISA, Ranchi, Jharkhand , and ICAR-CIRCOT, Mumbai, Maharashtra . The compostable material was processed at composting facilities for preparation of organic manure. The initiative resulted in the cleaning and segregation of biodegradable waste generated during Ganesh Visarjan and its conversion into a useful resource through composting.
The activities contributed to promoting awareness on cleanliness, sanitation, environmental protection and responsible waste management, while encouraging the adoption of clean, safe and environmentally responsible practices during and after Ganesh Visarjan.
